title: Rirena Arama's Whakakoro F4 shares: 2.178 in 1936 but 6.534 by c. 1988
side_a: Succession schedule (doc 1517478): Rirena Arama took 1/15 = 2.178 shares of Peri Paraihe's 32.667 in 1936
side_b: Owner list c. 1988 (doc 1279748): "Rirena Rihari Matiu (Mrs Arama)" 6.534 shares; also 6.534 shares on the current title (S06)
hypothesis: 6.534 = 3 × 2.178: Rirena later succeeded to the shares of her brother Tame and sister Whina Rihari Matiu (both presumably died without issue after 1960). Look for succession orders to Tame and Whina Rihari Matiu, 1960–1988, in Whakakoro F4 (and the other Peri Paraihe blocks). SUPPORT: in Rotokakahi A3B1B1B Whina's whole share passed solely to Rirena on 9 Nov 1970 (doc 1279339, KT 6/315). A parallel order for Tame (alias Manuera Rihari Matiu) has not yet been seen.

title: Maraea's children: 1936 whakapapa names Rirena, Tame and Whina only; Paihia 1D1E2 shows Hira and Rata Rihari Matiu as equal owners with Rirena
side_a: Minute book 15 HK 261 (doc 1650181), whakapapa supplied 25.9.36: Maraea = Rihari Matiu → Rirena Arama, Tame Rihari Matiu, Whina Rihari Matiu
side_b: Paihia 1D1E2 owner list (doc 1284640): Hira Rihari Matui 5.318, Rata Rihari Matui 5.317, Rirena Rihari Matiu or Rirena Arama 5.317 — equal shares; whānau records: Hira's 1913 birth certificate names Maraea as mother
hypothesis: The 1936 whakapapa was limited to those succeeding to Peri Paraihe (Maraea's side) — Hira and Rata may have been omitted deliberately, been whāngai, or be children of Rihari Matiu by another mother; alternatively the Paihia 1D1E2 shares came through Rihari Matiu (Wiripo line), not Maraea. Check the Paihia 1D1E2 title order / partition minute for the source of the six 5.317 shares, and the 1936 minute for objections.

title: Tura (Hāre Hongi) and Hare Hongi Hika's 1890 successions — resolved: "Tura Wiremu" is named in both Waihapa and Otangaroa
side_a: Whānau whakapapa: Tura Wiremu Tangata / Tura Hāre Hongi is a child of Hāre Hongi Hika (T016)
side_b: Otangaroa No 1 register (doc 1439296): the third successor, first read as "Piera Wiremu m.", is "Tura Wiremu" (a stray tick over the T; the Waihapa register, doc 1492723, has "Tura Wiremu f." in the same list of 27.2.90).
hypothesis: Resolved as a reading error. Tura Wiremu succeeded to her father Hāre Hongi Hika in Waihapa (27.2.90, with Rongo Kahira, Mereana Paora, Rati Pona, Wini Tuta, Huia Miriama, Arihia Hemi, Poni Rewharewha) and Otangaroa No 1 (28.2.90, with Rongo Kahira, Mereana Paora, Rati Poni, Wini Tuta, Meti Toetoe). The Otangaroa clerk wrote "m." against her name in error.

title: Two Rirenas: Rirena Arama Taniora (daughter of Arama Taniora, b. c. 1912) and Rirena Theresa Arama née Rihari Matiu (wife of Wiremu Arama, b. c. 1911)
side_a: Taupo 23C 1932 (doc 1527268) and 2009 (doc 3844962): "Rirena Arama Taniora", f., one of Arama Taniora and Peti Wiremu Tangata's eight children, coming of age 1933
side_b: Paihia 1D1E2 and Whakakoro F4: "Rirena Rihari Matiu or Rirena Arama" — Rirena Theresa, daughter of Rihari Matiu and Maraea, married Wiremu Arama 1928, d. 1980
hypothesis: Two different women, sister-in-law and wife of Wiremu Arama, both recorded as "Rirena Arama" in some documents. Any record citing "Rirena Arama" without a patronym or block context must be checked against both: interests derived from Taniora Rihari / Arama Taniora belong to Rirena Arama Taniora; interests derived from Peri Paraihe / Rihari Matiu / Matiu Wiripo belong to Rirena Theresa. The 1981 succession to Rirena in Paihia 1D1E2 (a Wiripo-line block) is Rirena Theresa's.
note: Case-manager alert — alias collision across two lines.

title: Paraihe parents and siblings: Moengaroa (Paraihe, d. by 1889), Wiremu/Wi Paraihe (d. 1891), Mereana Paraihe (d. by 1896), Te Hemowai Pirini — how they fit around Hone Paraihe
side_a: Rotokakahi A register (doc 1491535): both succeeded 16.3.96 by Peri Paraihe, Hira Amuketi and Mereana Pirini equally; Owhata A schedule (doc 1487280): Moengaroa (Paraihe) succeeded 13.11.89 by Peri Paraihe, Wi Paraihe, Hira Amuketi and Te Hemowai Pirini equally
side_b: Whakakoro F4 schedule (doc 1517478): Hone Paraihe succeeded 28.4.14 by the same three (Hira via her children) — Hone is the father
hypothesis: Wi/Wiremu Paraihe was a co-successor in 1889 and himself succeeded by the other three in 1896 — a sibling. Moengaroa (1889) and Mereana Paraihe (1896) were each succeeded by the siblings equally — one is likely the mother (Hone Paraihe's wife), the other possibly a sister, or the same woman under two names. Te Hemowai Pirini (1889) is probably Mereana Pirini (1896, 1914) under another name. Check the 1889 Owhata and 1896 Rotokakahi A minutes.
note: Provisional: Moengaroa entered as Hone Paraihe's wife; Wiremu and Mereana Paraihe as his children.

title: Taniora Rihari: "Himi Taniora, d. 1918" (Tauaki, N66A/100) vs "Taniora Rihari or Rihari Taniora, d. 1922" (Taupo 23C, N66A/99) — same person or two brothers?
side_a: Tauaki schedule (doc 1526207 p.4): deceased "Himi Taniora", N66A/100, 1918; order 29.2.32; 29 successors in sevenths
side_b: Taupo 23C schedule (doc 1527268): "Taniora Rihari or Rihari Taniora", N66A/99, 1922; same 29 successors; Taupo ownership schedule (doc 1527452) heads the entry "Himi Taniora Rihari"
hypothesis: Consecutive minute-book entries (N66A/99 and /100) at the same sitting with identical successors point to one person under two recorded names — Himi Taniora Rihari — with the year of death recorded inconsistently (1918 / 1922). Alternatively Himi was a brother who died without issue, his interest going to Taniora Rihari's descendants. Check N66A/99–100.

title: Karikari 2 / Te Kohanga Matiu whānau (Matiu Paewoi, d. 1910) — related to Matiu Wiripo of Pawarenga?
side_a: Karikari 2 schedules (docs 1407032, 1407079): Matiu Paewoi d. 26.7.1910 → Reihana, Waata @ Raniera, Wiremu, Tiini @ Riwhi, Miriama and Toni @ Heni Matiu (1922); Kiritiana Matiu d. 1936; the same family (plus Miha, Whinia, Queenie Matiu) on Te Kohanga at Ahipara (doc 1391616).
side_b: Map: Matiu Wiripo (T010, 1856–1931, son of Wiripo Te Moki, of Rotokakahi/Pawarenga) with children Rihari, Atama, Wiremu Matiu, Reta Waipouri and (probably) Ruhia and Pirini. A Wiremu Matiu appears in both families.
hypothesis: No document yet links the two families; the Karikari Wiremu Matiu is a son of Matiu Paewoi, so the Karikari and Te Kohanga records are attached to no tupuna. If the Karikari and Te Kohanga folders were collected because of a known descent from Matiu Paewoi or Kiritiana Matiu, say so and the attributions can be made.
note: Opened from the Karikari/Te Kohanga transcriptions.

title: Parengarenga B3: Kaperiera, Manuera, Merata and Mikahere Matiu (6.733 shares each) — children of Rihari Matiu? Rihari Matiu himself absent from the B3 list
side_a: Parengarenga B3 owners list c. 1970 (doc 1459641): Kaperiera Matiu (84), Manuera Matiu (103), Merata Matiu (125), Mikahere Matiu (136) with equal 6.733/6.734 shares — four co-heirs of one Matiu; beside them Aterea, Hera, Kaperiera, Manuera and Matuku Waipouri and Matiu Pereeme (40.637). No Rihari Matiu under R.
side_b: LINZ/MLC search (S06): Rihari Matiu owns 4.417 shares in Parengarenga B3A (NA55A/1289, partition order 1.8.1973). Rihari Matiu d. 1949, "remarried several times"; his son Tame is recorded as "Tame @ Manuera Rihari Matiu" (T025).
hypothesis: Either the four Matiu are Rihari Matiu's children by a later marriage who succeeded to his B3 interest before the 1973 partition (and the B3A title carries an older name), or they are an unrelated Matiu family of Te Aupōuri. The Waipouri names beside them match Reta Waipouri (T142) and Annie Theresa Waipouri (T124) in the Rotokakahi/Taupo records. Check the B3A succession file and the two large Parengarenga records (docs 1554588, 1282585) once they can be read. CHECK 29.9.26: "Kaperiera" occurs in none of the 13 Karikari records (all read) nor in the Te Kohanga 1965 list (K-section by OCR: Kapeti Wi Hamiora → Katene Raukawa Motu, no Kaperiera); it occurs only on Parengarenga B3 — Kaperiera Matiu (6.733) and Kaperiera Waipouri (2.110). Kaperiera = Kaperiere, the alias of Peri Paraihe; Ruhia Matiu Wiripo's children were recorded as "… Peri Matiu" (docs 1488165), so a Kaperiera Matiu sits in the Pawarenga (Matiu Wiripo) naming, not the Karikari (Matiu Paewoi) family, whose members (Reihana, Waata @ Raniera, Tiini @ Riwhi, Miha, Heni, Miriama, Karaitiana, Patana, Mei) share no name with the Parengarenga four. He is not among Peri Paraihe's sons on the 1936 order (Hone, Okena, Pirini, Arapeta), so a grandson or nephew named for him is the likelier reading.

title: "Rihipeti Arama" of Te Kohanga — the 1896 successor of Hamiora (d. 1922) and the 24.405-share owner of 1965: Erihapeti Arama née Wiremu Tangata, or a kuia she was named after?
side_a: Te Kohanga owners list under the partition order of 10.3.1965 (doc 1391616): no. 272 Rihipeti Arama f. 24.405 — one of the larger interests in a block at Ahipara. RESOLVED FOR TE KOHANGA No. 1 (6 Oct 2026, doc 1391476 read in full): a Rihipeti Arama succeeded on 5 Sep 1896 (N 17/47) to Hamiora Rungaiterangi alias Hamiora (original owner no. 18), 1/3 each with Hariata Haimona and Te Wikiriwhi Poutu; she died 17 Dec 1922 and her .334 passed solely to Eruera Paora (Wahapu) on 21 Feb 1925, then to his four successors in 1944. She is not on the 1963 Te Kohanga 1 compiled list.
side_b: Map: Erihapeti / Peti Wiremu Tangata, Mrs Arama (T004, 1880–1960), recorded on Pokaka A and Te Pupuke J1 (Whangaroa) and as trustee on Taupo 23C; no Ahipara interest recorded. NEW (6 Oct 2026): a BDM death certificate (reg. 1887002164, certified copy issued 27 Feb 2025) for Renata Tangata — Church of England clergyman, b. c. 1837 at Ahipara, d. 6 Apr 1887 at Mangonui (jury verdict: an unidentified poison), buried 9 Apr 1887 at "Aria"; parents Himiona Tangata and Hopereau; wife Harata Hereti (m. Auckland); one daughter aged 17 — puts a Himiona Tangata whānau at Ahipara, where Te Kohanga lies. Wiremu Tangata (T006, b. 1861, father recorded as Tangiwhare) is a generation younger than Renata.
hypothesis: Weighing the whānau context against the record: (1) Haimona and Himiona are the same name (Simon/Simeon), so "Hariata Haimona" = Hariata Himiona is sound; Hamiora (Samuel) is a different name and the clerk wrote it twice, but a slip is possible. (2) The chronology, not the spelling, is what separates the Te Kohanga No. 1 woman from Erihapeti: she succeeded as an adult in 1896 (no age recorded — Erihapeti, b. 1880, would have been entered as a minor of 16) and died 17 Dec 1922, while Peti Wiremu Tangata was appointed trustee on 29 Feb 1932 and took a succession on 20 Jul 1949. She is therefore at most a kuia Erihapeti was named after — e.g. a daughter of Arama Te Patara (T148) and so an aunt of Arama Taniora, which would make Te Kohanga No. 1 land of the Te Patara/Arama line on the husband's side; or an Arama woman who married a Paora, Eruera Paora (Wahapu) being her only child (he took solely). (3) The Paora link to Pokaka is not borne out by the records held: the Paora beside Wiremu Tangiwhare in Pokaka group B (1895) is Paora Patete Heke of the Heke/Ururoa whānau; the Paora in group A beside Tura is Mereana Paora = Mereana Hongi, Tura's sister, widow of Pera Paora (d. 1901; children Miraka, Paora, Marnea(?), Mereihe — no Eruera). Eruera Paora Wahapu appears in no Pokaka, Pupuke, Otangaroa or Waihapa record. (4) The record that could carry Erihapeti herself is the 1965 Te Kohanga (Lots 1, 3–27) list: its "Rihipeti Arama 24.405" is not inherited from No. 1 and sits unsucceeded in 1965 — exactly what an owner who died in 1960 would look like. It comes from another parent block of the 1965 amalgamation (Te Kohanga 2 or 3), and that is where a Himiona Tangata / Renata Tangata derivation would show. Next: the Te Kohanga 2/3 owner lists and the 1965 amalgamation order (P.O. 10.3.65) from Pātaka Whenua; and the whānau line and dates of Hariata Rongo, to test her against the adult Hariata Haimona of 1896.
note: Opened from the Te Kohanga transcription. Whānau context (6 Oct 2026): Hamiora/Himiona and Haimona/Himiona may be clerical variants; Hariata Rongo is Erihapeti's great-grandmother in the whānau whakapapa; Eruera Paora is said to be of the Paora line on Pokaka beside Wiremu Tangiwhare.

title: "Himi Ngawati Taitimu or Himi Wikitangi Taitimu" (Te Puna Topu o Hokianga, d. by 1986; Martha Adams executrix) — a son of Taitimu (Wereta) Arama Taniora alias Tim Adams?
side_a: Te Puna Topu o Hokianga schedule (doc 1559797): list 253 Himi Ngawati Taitimu or Himi Wikitangi Taitimu, .283 shares; s.81/67 4.3.86 → Martha Adams as executrix, then Martha Adams solely.
side_b: Map: Taitimu Arama Taniora / Tim Adams (T107, b. c. 1911) with children Rosie Adams, Hinemoa Adams and Annie Theresa Waipouri (1980 succession, Taupo 23C); Ruhia Matiu Wiripo also carried the name "Ruhia Paura Taitimu" (T023).
hypothesis: "Taitimu" as a surname plus an Adams executrix suggests the Arama/Adams line (Arama = Adams), but Himi is not among the 1980 Taupo 23C successors of Tim Adams and no order names his parents. Treat as a lead, not a link, until the Te Puna Topu succession file (RN 8/71–72) is read.
note: Opened from the Te Puna Topu transcription.

title: Waimate North A & B: six Rihari (incl. "Manga Rihari") and the Kingi set under 1 WH(S) 209 (incl. "Peti Kingi") — the Taniora Rihari line?
side_a: Waimate North A & B list, 1990s (doc 1273080): Aropai, Hiiripanga, Hori, Manga, Reipa and Taku Rihari at 0.630/0.631 each; Gwen, Huirua, Hunia, Kororiria, Peti, Taki and Te Whareumu Kingi at 0.0531 each (1 WH(S) 209); none of them on the earlier A and B schedules (docs 1515373, 1515383).
side_b: Map: Manga Taniora Rihari (T091, d. by 1962) and Peti Kingi (T116, trustee 1932) in the Taniora Rihari line, whose lands are Taupo 23C, Tauaki and Mangaiti (Whangaroa), c. 30 km north-west of Waimate North.
hypothesis: Same names, later generation: the Waimate North Rihari and Kingi are 1990s successors and could be grandchildren of the Whangaroa families — or Ngāpuhi families of the same names. Nothing here supports an attribution; kept as a lead.
note: Opened from the Waimate North index.

title: "Mori Takorekore Nepia Reewe or Mrs Mita King" (Karikari 2 / 2D) — wife of Mita Heremaia Kingi?
side_a: Karikari 2 (doc 1407032, 1960) and Karikari 2D (doc 1265151): Mori Takorekore (Takekore) Nepia Rewe @ Mrs Mita King, daughter of Nepia Rewi, 8.333 → 12.500 shares, sold to Waiheke Bailey 1977.
side_b: Map: Mita Heremaia Kingi (T114, b. c. 1903), grandson of Taniora Rihari, 1/14 successor in Taupo 23C (1932), still on the 2009 list.
hypothesis: "Mita King" = Mita Kingi is plausible for a Whangaroa/Ngāti Kahu marriage of the 1930s–50s, but no record here names Mita King's parents. If confirmed it would give the Kingi line a Karikari connection.

title: Wainui / Matauri: "Hira Matiu", mother of the Moana Hira children (b. c. 1890) — a sister of Rihari Matiu, or an unrelated Whangaroa Matiu?
side_a: Wainui D succession 29.2.32 (doc 1468358, N66A/129): Wiremu Haare / Wi Haare (d. 1922) → Rena and Hokena Wiremu Hare 1/3 each and Muiri, Katipua, Ani and Moana Moana Hira 1/12 each — the four children of a deceased son (Moana Wiremu Haare) and of Hira Matiu. The clerk writes the same four as "Moana Hira Matiu", "Ani Hira Matiu", "Muiri Haare" (1941, N 72/757), and on the 1958 Wainui A list as "Ani Moana Hira @ Ani Hira Matiu", "Muiri Moana Hira @ Muiri Hone Hira @ Muiri Hira Matiu", "Moana Moana Hira @ Pita Moana Hira @ Moana Hira Matiu"; Matauri X (1970): "Ani Hira Matiu or Ani Moana Hira" etc. Moana Moana Hira came of age in 1937 (b. c. 1916), so Hira Matiu was born c. 1885–1895. Wainui 2F (doc 1468443, 1905–17) gives the generation above: Haare Neke (d. 1905) and Wiremu Neke were the Neke brothers; Wiremu Neke's children were Hona, Haki and Hemi Wiremu and Atareta Hoori; Wi Haare / Wiremu Haare (d. 1922, the Moana Hira children's grandfather) is a separate man, the 1890 successor of Pataromu Tangaroa alongside Haare Neke and Matiu Pataromu.
side_b: Map: Matiu Wiripo (T010, 1856–1931, Rotokakahi/Pawarenga) with children Rihari (b. 1880), Atama/Okena, Wiremu, Reta Waipouri and (probably) Ruhia and Pirini — no Hira. Hira Rihari Matiu (T062, b. 1913, Paihia 1D1E2) is a generation too young to be this Hira. The Wainui/Matauri Haare, Kingi Hori, Kepa Tupe, Manahara and Ihaia families (docs 1537505, 1461969, 1375903, 1389221) are Whangaroa coast (Matauri Bay – Te Ngaere) whānau.
hypothesis: Three readings: (a) Hira Matiu was a daughter of Matiu Wiripo who married Moana Wiremu Haare of Wainui — which would make Hira Rihari Matiu (b. 1913) her namesake niece and give the Matiu Wiripo whānau a Whangaroa line beside the Taniora Rihari one; (b) she was a daughter of another Matiu (e.g. the Matiu Paewoi or Matiu Pataromu families of Karikari/Wainui — Matiu Pataromu succeeded Pataromu Tangaroa on Te Wainui in 1890, doc 1537505, so a "Hira Matiu" of Wainui could simply be his daughter); (c) "Hira Matiu" is itself a two-part personal name. Reading (b) has a documentary foothold on the block itself and is the more economical. Test: Hira Matiu's own succession order (she is not among the 1932–58 deceased, so she died before 1932 or after 1969) and the Matiu Pataromu line.
note: Opened from the Wainui records attached 4 Oct 2026.

title: "Hera Arama @ Hera Nako @ Hera Hona" of Wainui (b. c. 1904) and her son "Nako Arama Arama" — did a Nako daughter of Whangaroa marry an Arama (Taniora)?
side_a: Wainui records: Hera Nako, f 18, succeeded with her brothers Timohu (20), Noki (14) and Henare (10) to their mother Mate Nako (d. 1917) on Wainui D in 1922 (doc 1468358) and to their grandfather Harepeka Taharoa on Wainui 2E (doc 1468430); from the 1930s she is entered as "Hera Arama @ Hera Nako @ Hera Hona @ Hera Nako Hona" (N 75/251) and her sole successor is "Nako Arama Arama" (m), who also took 1/24 of Hone Taotahi's interest by exchange 27.2.47 and whose 35/192 went to Piri Mokena in 1955.
side_b: Map: Arama Taniora (T002, d. 1915) and Peti Wiremu Tangata's children include "Arama Taniora II or Honetiaki Arama Taniora" (T105, a minor in 1932, Taupo 23C/Tauaki) — a man who would be called "Arama Arama" in everyday use — and Wiremu Arama (T001, 1907–66). Taupo 23C and Tauaki are c. 10 km from Wainui/Matauri.
hypothesis: A son named Nako Arama Arama points to a father known as Arama Arama. Arama Taniora II (Honetiaki) is the obvious local candidate, which would make Hera Nako his wife and Nako Arama Arama a first cousin of Rirena Theresa Arama's children — but no record read so far names Hera's husband or Nako's father, and "Arama" is a common given name. Check Nako Arama Arama's own succession (after 1955) and the Taupo 23C/Tauaki files for a Nako Arama.
note: Opened from the Wainui 2E/2F schedules attached 4 Oct 2026.
